summary: Physics Lab office-table and filing-cabinet fixtures close their declared total mass exactly from component masses, but their declared centerOfMassM values disagree with the component mass-weighted centroids, leaving source-authored physical mass metadata internally inconsistent before F2/F3 promotion.
evidence: officeTable component masses sum exactly to declared massKg 27.0 kg: four 2.4 kg legs + 2.0 kg crossbar + 15.4 kg top. Their authored Y centroids yield (4*2.4*-0.03 + 2.0*0.15 + 15.4*0.33) / 27.0 = 0.1886666666666667 m, while centerOfMassM.y is declared as 0.08 m.

filingCabinet component masses sum exactly to declared massKg 36.6 kg: 24.0 kg shell + three 4.2 kg drawers. Their authored centroids yield COM y = 0.017213114754098358 m and z = -0.0034426229508196728 m, while centerOfMassM is declared as {x=0,y=-0.06,z=0.01}.

Existing rolling-cart repair PR #311 explicitly treats component-mass/centroid-derived COM coherence as a physical-authoring requirement, and chair adversarial PR #332 independently locks the same invariant for the chair; neither covers officeTable or filingCabinet.

Because these fixtures are used by the permanent Physics Lab and every ObjectGenome component is realized at F2, inconsistent declared COM metadata can become a different physical truth once later fidelity promotion consumes centerOfMassM for actuation/balance/handling.

metadata.recommendedAction: Recompute and version the officeTable and filingCabinet declared COMs from the authored component mass distribution, then add a fixture-wide deterministic regression that requires exact component-mass closure and component-derived COM coherence for all permanent Physics Lab ObjectGenomes whose component masses fully account for massKg.
